findings.affected_surface: Public GLib/GObject/GIO C API (public header glib/gquark.h)
findings.old_behavior: g_quark_to_string() was declared with G_GNUC_CONST (__attribute__((__const__))), telling the compiler the function does not read any global memory and its return value depends only on its arguments. This allows aggressive optimizations such as common subexpression elimination (CSE) — repeated calls with the same argument may be merged into a single call.
findings.new_behavior: g_quark_to_string() is now declared with G_GNUC_PURE (__attribute__((__pure__))), telling the compiler the function may read global memory (the quark table) but does not modify it. The compiler can still optimize some redundant calls but must account for the possibility that the global quark table has changed between calls.
findings.compatibility_reason: The G_GNUC_CONST annotation was incorrect because g_quark_to_string() reads the global quark hash table to resolve a GQuark to its string representation. Code compiled against the old header may have had calls to g_quark_to_string() optimized more aggressively (e.g., two calls with the same GQuark value could be merged into one). After recompilation against the new header, the compiler will emit additional calls to g_quark_to_string() that were previously optimized away. This could cause performance differences (more function calls executed) and, in pathological cases where the global quark table changed between the merged calls, different program behavior (the merged call would return the table's state at the time of the single call, whereas separate calls reflect per-call table state). The change is a correctness fix — the old annotation was technically wrong — but it is still a visible change in the public API declaration that affects how the compiler treats the function.

findings.why_not_internal_only: The change is in glib/gquark.h, which is a public header installed as part of GLib's public API. The g_quark_to_string() function is exported from the shared library and available to all consumers of GLib. The function attribute (G_GNUC_CONST vs G_GNUC_PURE) is visible to any code that includes this header and affects how the compiler generates code at every call site.
findings.uncertainty: Low uncertainty. The patch is small and well-documented; the semantic difference between __attribute__((const)) and __attribute__((pure)) is well-defined by GCC. The actual observable impact depends on compiler version, optimization level, and how aggressively callers rely on the const annotation for optimization. At -O0 there is no difference. At -O2 and above with LTO, the impact can be significant.
findings.recommended_review: No manual review needed. The patch is a straightforward annotation fix that makes the declaration match the function's actual semantics. The commit message is clear about the intent.
findings.test_recommendation: Low-priority testing recommendation: verify that g_quark_to_string() still returns correct results for typical GQuark values after recompilation. Since the change only affects compiler optimization semantics (not runtime behavior), standard GLib test suites covering string-to-quark and quark-to-string round-trips should suffice. Performance regression testing is optional.
findings.test_priority_reason: Low priority: The change is a correctness fix for an incorrect compiler annotation. It does not alter the function's runtime behavior, return values, input contract, or error handling. The observable effect is limited to compiler optimization decisions (potential additional function calls). The fix makes the declaration semantically correct — the previous annotation was technically wrong. Typical consumers recompiling against the new header will not experience functional breakage, though they may see minor performance differences at high optimization levels.
